core.title: Name appendix files {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename}
core.given: A plan artifact has, or needs, a supporting appendix file, regardless of where that file is stored.
core.when: The planner creates, renames or references that appendix file, or edits or reviews an existing appendix whose filename does not follow the pattern.
core.then: Name the file {artifact-name}_{type}_{filename}: the owning plan artifact's name first, one of the recognized appendix types second, a descriptive filename last, separated by underscores.
prefer: Use the owning plan artifact's exact name/id as the first segment.
Take {type} only from the recognized appendix types; look the list up rather than guessing.
Make {filename} descriptive of the content; hyphens may appear inside a segment.
When editing, reviewing or referencing an existing misnamed appendix, rename it to the pattern and update references to the new name.
avoid: Bare filenames missing the {artifact-name} and {type} segments.
Hyphens instead of underscores as segment separators.
Inventing a {type} value outside the recognized appendix types.
core.why: Encoding the owning artifact and appendix type in the filename ensures uniqueness, traceability back to the artifact, and clear type identification without opening the file.
evidence: Every appendix filename (created, renamed, edited, reviewed or referenced) splits on '_' into exactly three parts: artifact name, type, descriptive filename (+ extension).
The first part matches the name/id of an existing owning plan artifact.
The second part is one of the recognized appendix types.
verification: Filename check: every appendix filename in scope (created, renamed, edited, reviewed or referenced) splits on '_' into exactly three parts — owning artifact name, appendix type, descriptive filename plus extension; underscores are segment separators, hyphens may appear inside segments.

Segment checks: the {artifact-name} segment matches the name/id of an existing owning plan artifact of any kind (no owner-kind membership list); the {type} segment is one of the recognized appendix types supplied by the profile.

Appendix identity is not determined by path: the profile's appendix-storage location is only a non-exclusive, observable signal that a file is an appendix; the pattern applies to appendix files and appendix references anywhere, including existing misnamed appendices that are edited or reviewed.
The check does not cover which appendix type fits the content (governed by the stack's appendix-type convention) or where the appendix is stored (governed by the stack's appendix-storage convention).

Observability: create/rename/edit of a file is observable from the diff; a file under the profile's appendix-storage location is an observable appendix signal; appendix identity elsewhere and references to appendix filenames are llm_judged and may need a reference or filename-pattern observer (edit/review of a misnamed appendix fires only when the filename does not match).
No exceptions: `unless` is empty, so every appendix filename and reference in scope must match the pattern.

fires: The planner adds a new appendix file for an owning plan artifact, wherever it is stored.
The planner renames or moves an existing appendix file.
The planner edits or reviews an existing appendix whose filename does not match the pattern, even without renaming or referencing it.
A plan artifact, acceptance definition or other document references an appendix filename, whether the appendix is about to be created or already exists (including an existing misnamed appendix).
doesNotFire: Editing the content of an already correctly named appendix file without renaming or referencing it under another name.
Files that are not appendices (plan artifacts, acceptance definitions, production source code, tests), even if they sit near appendix files.
Choosing which appendix type applies (governed by the stack's appendix-type convention) or where to store it (governed by the stack's appendix-storage convention).

profileRequirements.meaning: The recognized appendix types; the {type} segment of an appendix filename may take only these values.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the six recognized appendix types listed in planner.appendix.types (e.g. mockup, diagram, spreadsheet)

profileRequirements.meaning: Where the stack stores appendix files; files under this location are an observable, non-exclusive signal that a file is an appendix. The storage location never limits scope: appendices stored or referenced elsewhere remain fully covered.

neutralityNotes: The naming obligation itself ({artifact-name}_{type}_{filename} with underscore separators, hyphens allowed inside segments) is filename-level and fully stack-neutral. (1) Owner kinds: bun.json's wagon/WMBT/feature/component are explicitly illustrative and non-exhaustive, so the core applies to appendices owned by any plan artifact; no owner-kind membership is required or profiled, and the examples remain only in the Bun reference text. (2) The 'six recognized appendix types' and the pointer 'planner.appendix.types' are stack data; the closed vocabulary has no key, so tooling.appendix_formats#types is proposed and the core defers to the profile's list. (3) The **/appendices/** storage heuristic is stack layout data and is explicitly non-exclusive; the vocabulary has no appendix-location key, so layout.locations#appendix_storage is proposed — it supplies an observable appendix signal only, while the core keeps role-based (llm_judged) appendix identity that applies wherever the appendix is stored or referenced, so scope is never limited by location. (4) Concrete positive/negative examples and the term id naming_pattern remain in the Bun realization, which is delivered as the worked reference example. The source declares no automated detector (implementation: none), so the core's verification describes review/LLM-judged checking generically.
